meta.title: macos-keyboard-backlight, script the MacBook keyboard backlight
meta.description: macOS gives you a slider and two keys, and no way to script either one. This adds a kbdlight command and a Node API to read and set the keyboard backlight and toggle the ambient light sensor. One dependency, no native build step, MIT.

hero.eyebrow: No build step, one dependency, MIT
hero.headline: Your keyboard backlight, finally scriptable.
hero.sub: macOS gives you a slider in System Settings and two keys on the keyboard, and that is the whole interface. There is no way to reach the keyboard backlight from a shell script, a scheduled job, or a Node program. This adds the missing one.

demo.heading: See it run
demo.alt: A lit MacBook keyboard seen from above. The command kbdlight auto off && kbdlight off runs, and the backlight drains away key by key.
demo.caption: The command is real and does exactly this. The MacBook is an illustration: the backlight is hardware, so no screen recording can show it.

why.heading: Why this exists
body: Almost every part of a Mac can be driven from a script. The keyboard backlight cannot: there is no command, no flag and no supported API. If you want it off between midnight and seven, or dimmed while a recording runs, there is nothing to call.
This package resolves the private CoreBrightness interface at runtime and exposes it as a command and a library, so the backlight becomes one more thing your scripts can control.
why.highlight: No node-gyp. No Xcode. Nothing compiled at install time.

items.title: A real command
items.body: kbdlight get, set, off, max, auto and list. Values are clamped to the 0.0 to 1.0 range before they reach the system call.

items.title: No native build step
items.body: No node-gyp, no Xcode, no compiler on the installing machine. The system calls are resolved at runtime through koffi, which ships prebuilt for both architectures.

items.title: A Node API too
items.body: get, set, isAuto and setAuto each take an optional keyboard ID, so you can target one keyboard instead of all of them. keyboardIDs() returns the IDs to pass them.

items.title: Honest failure
items.body: It calls a private Apple framework, so it throws a descriptive Error rather than crashing when that interface is not there. Catch it, do not feature-detect it.

items.title: The sensor gotcha, documented
items.body: Auto-brightness keeps re-adjusting the backlight and overrides a level you set. Turn the sensor off first and the value sticks. The help text says so too.

items.title: One dependency
items.body: koffi, and nothing else. Tested on macOS against Node 18, 20, 22 and 24 on every push.

install.heading: Install and use
install.intro: Requires macOS, Apple Silicon or Intel, and Node 18 or newer.

steps.title: Install
steps.body: Installs a kbdlight command. Use npx instead if you only want to run it once.

steps.title: Turn it off
steps.body: Disable the ambient sensor first, otherwise it adjusts the backlight straight back.

steps.title: Use it from Node
steps.body: The same operations as the command, returning numbers and booleans.

install.note: Restore the ambient light sensor at any time with kbdlight auto on.
